title: Runtime slice generator + ABI scan for per-model artifact bundles and gated rollouts
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Problem: Our canonical runtime image includes components not required by every model (extra Python packages, multiple CUDA helper libs, heavy OS tooling). This increases image size, boot latency, vulnerability surface, and complicates driver/CUDA compatibility matrices. We currently rely on coarse image pinsets and manual SBOM curation which slows rollouts and forces conservative LTS gates.

Goal: Build a Runtime Slice Generator (RSG) that produces minimal per-model runtime bundles (image or OCI index) and an automated ABI compatibility scanner that verifies driver/CUDA/libc/cuDNN compatibility for each slice. Each slice must have a machine-readable SBOM, a deterministic tag, and metadata linking it to the canonical build pipeline. Integrate generated slices into our release gating: canary (Dedicated small cohort) -> expanded canary -> LTS channel promotion.

Key outcomes: reduced per-model image size (target 25% median reduction for smaller models), per-slice SBOMs for fine-grained vulnerability and provenance checks, automated compatibility checks to prevent kernel/driver/ABI skews from hitting production, and rollout gates that use slice metrics instead of broad-image metrics.

Technical approach: iterate on three deliverables in parallel: 1) Slice generator: tooling that takes a canonical runtime artifact and a model spec and performs static and dynamic dependency pruning (layer flattening optional), producing an OCI image index and SBOM (CycloneDX); 2) ABI scanner: cross-checks binary symbols, CUDA driver API usage, and kernel module version requirements against a curated compatibility matrix and runs a lightweight test harness (smoke-run with KV-cache and perf microbenchmarks) in CI; 3) Gating integration: extend release orchestrator to accept slice metadata, run slice-specific smoke suites in canary Dedicated pools, and enforce promotion rules (failure thresholds, vulnerability delta limits).

Why different from prior work: instead of global pinsets or monolithic SBOM updates, we generate targeted bundles per workload and tie SBOMs + ABI checks to rollout decisions. This reduces blast radius and enables faster, safer upgrades of drivers and runtimes for particular model families.
acceptance_criteria: RSG prototype produces a reproducible OCI index for two sample model specs (gpt-small, reranker) with CycloneDX SBOM attached
ABI scanner flags incompatibilities by symbol/API mismatch and fails CI when thresholds exceeded
Slice metadata is consumed by the release orchestrator and used to gate a canary rollout in Dedicated (test cohort: 5 clusters)
End-to-end run (build -> slice -> abi-scan -> canary deploy -> smoke tests) completes in CI pipeline with documented logs and a dashboard tile
Documentation: Confluence design doc, runbook for operators, and a public PRD for PM/Design review
tasks: Design doc: detail slice format, SBOM fields, provenance tags (owner/model-spec/hash)
Prototype RSG: dependency collector (static pip/apt/cpp libs) and prune pass; emit OCI index + CycloneDX
Implement ABI scanner: symbol extractor, CUDA API usage checker, kernel/driver heuristic checks
Add CI jobs: slice-build, abi-scan, smoke-run; integrate artifacts into artifact-registry with signed attestations
Extend release orchestrator to accept slice metadata and enforce promotion rules (configurable thresholds)
Create canary cohort in Dedicated for slice rollout tests and add telemetry collection (startup latency, error rate, token throughput)
Write runbook for rollback + emergency pinning of canonical image if slice causes regressions
Security review and SBOM signing flow + KMS integration
